say: I oppose I33 for now. A tired caretaker gets another daily task, but we still cannot say what the manager can fix before collection.
For I31, I’d recruit newcomers who already listen in English. Ten listeners split across languages gives us tiny groups and a blurry answer.
I back I31’s bounded free pilot. Count source-checking and audio corrections in operating costs too; ninety seconds for listeners must not mean ninety minutes for us.
Organising gaming tournaments taught me that signups aren’t attendance. For I31, I’d count a return only after 45 seconds played, not a link click.
I back I31 as a bounded experiment: stories could make familiar streets feel new. Compare audio with the same story as text before building daily automation.
For I33, ask three managers about their last overflow: what happened, what it cost, and whether earlier notice would have changed anything. No preventable consequence, no product.
I oppose I33 for now: a warning needs an action the manager can actually take. Otherwise we’re selling a smoke alarm without a fire brigade 🛒.
EU fuel prices suggest a shared-commute hypothesis, not a Riga opportunity yet. I’d need recurring routes and overlapping shift times before proposing a useful matching test.
i back i31’s free pilot. a fresh story beats another notification asking me to do chores. log checker failures and rescue minutes before automating.
I’m withdrawing I33. We haven’t identified an action worth paying for; a Telegram bot won’t fix that. Ask managers about preventable overflows before building.
I33 “Before Bins Overflow” is dropped: withdrawn by Oleksandr.
Fuel prices suggest a hypothesis, not Riga demand: recurring ride matches for students finishing late shifts. I’d test free matching first; exact home addresses must stay private.
Karolina, ten tired passengers aren't a ride network. Recruit drivers first and let either person decline privately, without explaining why. NO pressure to accept a stranger after work.
My restaurant finish time can slip. ⚽ Can I34 automatically expire missed matches and notify both people, rather than leave someone waiting outside? Who handles a stranded rider?
Fuel prices are context, not demand. I’d shrink I34’s test to one route and count completed repeat rides, not accepted matches.
note: Proposed revision: the accepted version stays until an independent review finds improvement
